title: Redefine surface depth tokens and responsive type metrics for dense dashboard widgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate and update the design token set for surface elevations, shadow layers, spacing/radius, and a responsive typography scale targeted at dense dashboard and data table contexts. The goal is to provide a predictable visual hierarchy across compact widgets, charts, and table rows while improving contrast and accessibility for low-vision scenarios.
rationale: Recent customer feedback and internal console analytics show that dense data surfaces (widgets, tables, inline charts) suffer from indistinct surface layering and cramped typographic rhythm at small sizes. This leads to mistaken affordances and slower scanning. A focused token update will enable consistent composition rules, simplify engineering variants, and reduce the number of local overrides in apps.
decisions: Introduce a 6-step elevation palette (surface-0..surface-5) with explicit use-cases documented (background, card, raised-card, floating, overlay, modal).
Normalize shadow expressions to two system shadow tokens mapped to hardware-accelerated CSS variables for better perf on low-end devices.
Create a compact typography ramp (compact-xs, compact-sm, compact-md, base) optimized for 10–14px readable metrics with adjusted line-heights and optical letter-spacing.
Add small-radius variants (r-2, r-4) to token set for dense controls and micro-interactions while preserving existing radius tokens for larger surfaces.
Define a contrast augmentation guideline (+contrast token variants) for critical text on dense surfaces to ensure AA at small sizes.
Ship tokens as single-source JSON and CSS custom properties; provide a migration guide for component library and existing product surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Token file added: design-tokens/density-v2.json and published to the token registry.
Figma components updated and annotated with usage specs for each surface token and compact type ramp.
Console widget and table stories updated in the component library demonstrating new tokens at three breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) with visual diffs.
Automated contrast checks in the design system repo pass for primary and secondary text on all surface elevations at compact sizes.
Migration guide created describing how to replace local overrides with tokenized values and rollout schedule for Product teams.
tasks: Audit current components for local color/shadow overrides and produce a list of top 25 occurrences.
Author new token JSON and CSS variable mappings.
Update Figma library: surface styles, shadow styles, compact type styles, radius tokens.
Create component library PR with token usage in Button, TableRow, Card, ChartContainer.
Write migration guide and sample codemod for common override patterns.
Coordinate rollout with Platform and Docs: schedule canary release and deprecation notices.
engineering_notes: Prefer CSS custom properties mapped to runtime tokens so Dedicated/Private deployments can override at region/tenant scope.
Shadow tokens should prefer single-layer drops with GPU friendly transforms; avoid expensive layered box-shadows where possible.
Provide a tokens.json and a tokens.css export. Coordinate version bump with Console team to avoid layout regressions.
Add unit tests that validate token presence and run visual regression snapshots for the affected component stories.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish token set and update Figma library; internal design review and accessibility validation.
Week 2: Implement token hooks in component library and open PR; smoke test console staging with canary flag.
Week 3: Gradual rollout to product teams with opt-in; collect usage metrics and visual regression results.
Week 4: Default flip for non-critical surfaces; schedule follow-up for any high-contrast exceptions.
